question: How hard does the rocket accelerate off the pad?

report.answer: The SLS climbs straight up with a net upward acceleration of about 5.1 m/s², about 0.52 g. Fitted as a projectile this appears as g = -5.07 m/s² — i.e. powered flight, not free fall. This matches the published SLS Block 1 figures: ~39 MN liftoff thrust on a ~2,600 t vehicle gives T/W ~1.5, or T/W-1 ~0.5 g net.
assumptions: Camera fixed on tripod, no zoom during climb
Motion in vertical plane facing camera, no strong perspective change
Scale from SLS Block 1 height 98.1 m +/- 3.0 m side-on, at same depth as motion

forks.label: No air
forks.why: At these low speeds drag is negligible; shows same climb to isolate thrust vs aero.

forks.label: Same rocket on Moon
forks.why: Keep thrust, lower weight: T/W ~9, net acceleration ~8 g — shows how much of liftoff struggle is Earth gravity.
